# Fixture tree manifest — `tests/fixtures/tree/`

Generated by [`../../scripts/make-fixtures.py`](../../scripts/make-fixtures.py) (deterministic:
same bytes, same name bytes, same modes, same mtimes on every run).
Rebuild with:

```sh
python3 scripts/make-fixtures.py --root tests/fixtures/tree --archives tests/fixtures/archives
# capture tree (hostile modes + 10 000-entry case + FIFO), used by capture-golden.sh:
python3 scripts/make-fixtures.py --root /tmp/zm-fix/tree --archives /tmp/zm-fix/archives \
    --hostile --fifo --with-heavy
```

All fixture mtimes are pinned to `1767225600` = `2026-01-01T00:00:00Z`
(`FIXTURE_MTIME`), including symlink and directory mtimes, so `mod_time` in the
golden `/api/dir` captures is reproducible. `future.txt` is
`FIXTURE_MTIME + 10 years`.

## What is checked in vs. what is generated

Git cannot store these four cases, so `--hostile` applies them at capture time and
`--relax` (also run by `capture-golden.sh` before it wipes the tree) restores a
walkable repository:

| case | committed state | capture state |
|---|---|---|
| `noperm.bin` | regular file, mode `0000` — what `make-fixtures.py` leaves in the working tree (git itself can only record `0644`/`0755`, so a fresh checkout is `0644` until the generator is run) | mode `0000` |
| `noread-dir/` | mode `0755` | mode `0000` (unreadable dir → `ReadDirNames` partial result) |
| `noexec-dir/` | mode `0755` | mode `0444` (readable, non-traversable) |
| `myfifo` | **absent** (git has no FIFO object) | created by `--fifo` |
| `flatcap/` (10 005 files, the flat-walk cap) | **absent** (never commit 10 k files) | created by `--with-heavy` |

## Entries (repo copy, mode as stored)

| name (as a Python bytes-literal repr of the UTF-8 name) | kind | mode | size | why it exists |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `.hidden` | file | 0644 | 15 | hidden file: the Go backend **never** filters dotfiles (§2.3 quirk 6) |
| `normal.txt` | file | 0644 | 14 | baseline regular file |
| `executable.sh` | file | 0755 | 18 | exec bit → `mode: "-rwxr-xr-x"` in `fileMode` strings |
| `a9.txt`, `a10.txt` | files | 0644 | 3, 4 | byte-compare on lowercased names ⇒ `a10.txt` sorts before `a9.txt` (quirk 2) |
| `SortCase/B.txt`, `SortCase/a.txt` | files | 0644 | 2, 2 | `'B'` (0x42) < `'a'` (0x61) ⇒ `B.txt` first ascending, even though `a` < `b` case-insensitively |
| `"weird\rname.txt"` | file | 0644 | 13 | **CRLF in name** — built as `"we" + "ird" + CR + "name.txt"`, verified with `ls \| od -c`; JSON-escaped as `\r` on the wire |
| `café.txt` (U+00E9, NFC) | file | 0644 | 16 | unicode, precomposed |
| `café.txt` (U+0065 U+0301, NFD) | file | 0644 | 12 | **combining char**: same *rendered* name, different bytes; both are listed and both survive the round trip |
| `日本.txt` | file | 0644 | 6 | non-latin name; `filepath.WalkDir` ordering and percent-encoding |
| `space name.txt` | file | 0644 | 6 | space ⇒ query encoding (`%20` vs `+`) |
| `hash#name.txt` | file | 0644 | 5 | `#` ⇒ naive string URL building would truncate the path |
| `quote'name.txt` | file | 0644 | 6 | `'` ⇒ shell/JSON escaping in `handleChmod`/`log` payloads |
| `back\slash.txt` | file | 0644 | 10 | `\` ⇒ Go `filepath.ToSlash` and the VFS `.zip/` substring guard |
| `very-long-name-xxxx…x.txt` (205 bytes) | file | 0644 | 5 | name > 200 chars: log codec field is `u16` length; UI ellipsis |
| `noperm.bin` | file | 0000 (repo *and* capture) | 11 | `chmod 000`: `lstat` still succeeds ⇒ listed with `mode: "----------"`, but `open`/read fails |
| `noread-dir/` (+ `inner.txt`) | dir | 0000 (capture) | — | directory without read permission: `/api/dir` ⇒ HTTP 500 `Failed to read directory` |
| `noexec-dir/` (+ `inner.txt`) | dir | 0444 (capture) | — | directory without execute permission: **HTTP 200** with degraded entries — see `tests/golden/dir-perm-noexec.json` |
| `link-to-file.txt → normal.txt` | symlink | 0777 | 10 | symlink to file: `is_dir:false`, `is_symlink:true`, `mode:"Lrwxrwxrwx"`, `size` = length of the target string (quirk 5) |
| `link-to-dir → subdir` | symlink | 0777 | 6 | symlink to **directory** — reported `is_dir:false` although `open` follows it |
| `link-chain.txt → link-to-file.txt` | symlink | 0777 | 16 | symlink-to-symlink chain (`lstat` still reports a symlink) |
| `broken-link → nowhere.txt` | symlink | 0777 | 11 | broken symlink: must appear in listings, must be openable-to-fail |
| `hard1.txt`, `hard2.txt` | files (nlink 2) | 0644 | 12, 12 | hard link pair: identical inode; the copy path must not double-count |
| `myfifo` (generated) | FIFO | 0644 | 0 | non-regular file: `mode:"prw-r--r--"`, `size:0` — a naive `open`+read would hang the UI thread |
| `future.txt` | file | 0644 | 16 | mtime 10 years ahead ⇒ date sort and "relative time" formatting with a negative delta |
| `sparse.bin` | file | 0644 | 1048576 | sparse: `size` (logical) vs `du` (≈4 KiB allocated) — a copy progress bar keyed on allocated bytes is wrong |
| `subdir/`, `subdir/a.txt`, `subdir/b/c.txt` | dirs/files | 0755/0644 | 2 each | dirs sort first regardless of name (§2.3 quirk 1) |
| `empty-dir/` | dir | 0755 | — | empty listing shape (`entries: []`, not `null`) |
| `deep/d0/…/d19/leaf.txt` | dirs/file | 0755/0644 | 9 | 20 nested levels + leaf ⇒ index `max_depth` (Go default `max_depth = 0` = unlimited, `search_index.go:100`) and `depth`/`rel_path` in flat listings |
| `many/f0001.txt … f1200.txt` | files | 0644 | 10 each | 1200 > Go page size **200** (`api/dir.go`: `limit := 200`) ⇒ 6 pages; `dir-many-p1/p2/last.json` |
| `fake.zip/inner.txt` | dir/file | 0755/0644 | 14 | a **real directory** ending in `.zip`: the VFS write guard is a substring test on `".zip/"` ⇒ writes there are refused (405) — see `tests/golden/err-vfs-readonly.json` |
| `flatcap/g00000.txt … g10004.txt` (generated) | files | 0644 | 1 each | 10 005 > 10 000: the flat walk stops at exactly `total_count: 10000` — see `tests/golden/dir-flat-cap.json` (quirk 4) |

## Deliberately NOT created

* **setuid binary** — skipped on purpose. A `chmod u+s` executable is either
  root-owned (needs `sudo`, which this capture must not use) or setuid to the
  unprivileged user, i.e. it grants nothing and only adds a repo artifact that
  `install(1)`/packagers will flag. `fs.FileMode.String()` renders the setuid bit
  as `ur-sr-xr-x`-style `s`/`S` in the *type* position; that mapping is covered by
  the Go-side table test in step 3 (`mode::Display` matches
  `fs.FileMode.String()`), which can synthesise the bit without a real setuid file.
* **`inner.7z` as a real 7z archive** — see `docs/contracts.md`, "Fixtures we
  cannot generate".

## Machine-readable manifest (generated — do not hand-edit)

Everything below is machine data. The block opens with a fence whose language tag
is `fixture-tree/1` and closes with the next bare fence. Each row is
`["<hex of the root-relative UTF-8 path>", "kind", "octal mode"]` with kind `f` file,
`d` directory, `l` symlink, `p` FIFO. Names are hex-encoded because the tree holds a
carriage return inside `weird\rname.txt` plus a `\`, a `#`, a `'`, and two `café.txt`
names that differ only in normalisation form (NFC vs NFD) — a markdown table cell
cannot be compared byte-exactly against a generated tree, so `cargo xtask fixture-tree`
parses this block instead of the tables above. Modes are the **repo** modes, i.e.
`make-fixtures.py` with no `--hostile` / `--fifo` / `--with-heavy`; `docs/fixtures.md` itself
is not part of the tree and is not listed. The gate regenerates the tree into a
throwaway directory under `target/` and diffs it against these rows.
